title: FizzBuzz as one switch expression

blocks.text: A switch expression is a value: it can be returned directly, and every arm gives one.
Write `say(int n)` in `FizzBuzz` as a single `return switch (...) { ... };`. It returns:

items: `"FizzBuzz"` when `n` is divisible by both 3 and 5;

blocks.text: Examples: `say(15)` is `"FizzBuzz"`, `say(9)` is `"Fizz"`, `say(10)` is `"Buzz"`, `say(7)` is `"7"`. The rules hold for every `int`: `say(0)` is `"FizzBuzz"`, `say(-3)` is `"Fizz"` and `say(-7)` is `"-7"`.
Hint: switch on the remainder by 15, and list several remainders in one arm.

cases.says: 15, 9, 10 and 7 give FizzBuzz, Fizz, Buzz and 7.
3, 6 and 12 are Fizz: every remainder that is a multiple of 3 is listed.
0 is FizzBuzz, -3 is Fizz and -10 is Buzz.

concepts: A switch expression yields a value that can be returned or assigned directly.
